title: P1-Q02 · Playtest-1 qualification, pinned preview, couch verdict
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-Q02** (cites §1, §13.4, §15 Q (playtest checklist); master §17.5 J01–J07, J10, J15 (reroll), J18); master cut V2-121, V2-44 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `PT1` · **Track:** `qual` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:owner`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** every other P1 task (102 beads; plan §15 Q). These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
The goal of the whole graph: the §1 story runs on the pinned "Playtest 1" preview with real phones (iOS and Android), host-local pads/keys, a
forced-TURN path and a direct LAN path, with receipts, and the owner's couch verdict (G-FEEL) recorded. Known gaps are listed, not hidden.
Depends on every other P1 task. The owner may run any checklist row on any preview at any time; each failed row becomes a bug bead citing it.

## Scope (owned paths)
`docs/playtests/round-<date>.md`, `docs/playtests/checklist.md`; pinning the preview (D06 workflow); the accepted baseline under `scenarios/accepted/<preview-id>/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Fixes for failed rows (new bug beads, probe-first, §13.4).

## Contract and design decisions
§1 story (the owner's playtest night): open the preview index, Host the pinned "Playtest 1" build on the laptop driving the TCL TV; 6–10 friends scan
the QR (or use the in-page scanner) and are driving within ~20 s (lobby warm-up or the tail of a running race); controls over WebRTC (direct on
home Wi-Fi when possible, coturn relay otherwise, Cloudflare only when neither works); numbered coloured Cruz Missiles in a dynamic grid with
Identify; three laps of a freshly generated four-biome track; doors/wheels go loose then fly off and stay as debris; wrecked cars respawn in
~2 s; mid-race joiners join at the back; a locked phone hands its car to autopilot and gets it back; results, highlight reel, next round on its
own; the host can End or Disband; afterwards a G-FEEL verdict and a round record. Development never stopped (R85).
Master §17.5 journeys at Playtest-1 scope: J01–J07, J10, J15 (reroll only), J18.

**Playtest checklist** (`docs/playtests/checklist.md`, real-device rows the owner runs):
| Area | Real-device row | From |
|---|---|---|
| Join | Open the index on the TV laptop and Host; an iPhone and an Android join by camera QR; the TV QR scans from 3 m; the in-page scanner works on iOS Safari and Android Chrome | G00, R07, C04 |
| Network | Phones on the home Wi-Fi go direct; a phone on cellular joins and its path (coturn or Cloudflare) is recorded; `tools/net/turn_probe.py` allocates on `turn.dilger.dev` from a phone hotspot; a client-isolated Wi-Fi if handy | G00, N04, N08, Q-N1 |
| Controls | Two thumbs on two sticks, no zoom/scroll/select; a hard left-stick swipe on an iPhone never navigates away; wake lock holds through a whole race; real pads on the TV host | C02, C03, C05 |
| Recovery | Lock a phone 30 s mid-race → same car within 3 s; a locked phone's car goes to autopilot and comes back | C03, G03 |
| Identity | Identify visible on the TV ≤ 150 ms after the press on LAN | R06 |
| Hosts | A phone hosts a 4-player race at ≥ 30 fps with sound; a weaker laptop hosts; frame pacing on the TCL at 4K; one quick host check (with sound) from Safari on the Mac and from a Windows PC when handy | R08, Q01, A03, §13.1 |
| Party | A newcomer gets through the tutorial; settings stick; a mid-race drop-in; voice and music on the TV | C06, C07, G02, A03 |
Owner actions feeding this: O6 (playtest night), O8 (playtest previews as they land), O9 (decide Q-N1 after a cellular playtest), O7 (§17.2
open questions). The owner's running to-do list per gate is `docs/playtests/owner-checklists.md`. The highlight reel (R09) isn't required here
(owner 2026-10-03); it ships when it lands.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: every other P1 bead. Provides: the G-FEEL verdict, repair list and accepted baseline (§13.4).

## Required tests
- The full milestone matrix (`batch-verify.sh run --matrix milestone`, F10) on the pinned build; the network (N08) and perf (Q01) receipts; the owner's checklist.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
Round record + checklist + receipts (`ev:owner`). Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-Q02/`.

## How this bead closes
- `ev:owner`: the owner's verdict in a round record (only P1-U04 and P1-Q02 use this).

## Working rules
Follow `AGENTS.md` (owner rules first) and `docs/process/bead-workflow.md`: check your own area, commit with `P1-Q02` and the bead ID in the message, push, and close this bead once CI is green on a commit containing it (gate pass, ticked items, `receipt:<run url>`).

## Anti-narrowing clause
> Done only when the FELT, observable outcome above holds in the RUNNING game via the real host path. Passing unit/geometry tests is necessary but NOT sufficient.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] [ev:owner] The §1 story runs on the pinned preview with real devices (iOS and Android phones, host-local pads/keys, a forced-TURN path and a direct LAN path).
- [ ] [ev:owner] Every checklist row passes or has an open bug bead the owner accepts as a known gap.
- [ ] [ev:owner] Network (N08) and perf (Q01) receipts are attached to the round record.
- [ ] [ev:owner] The owner's G-FEEL verdict and repair list are recorded in `docs/playtests/round-<date>.md`.
- [ ] [ev:owner] When the owner accepts the feel, the pinned build's affordance traces are committed as the accepted baseline (`scenarios/accepted/<preview-id>/`).
- [ ] Visual self-review done and committed (owner 2026-10-04): the device/state matrix was captured and every screenshot was looked at, defects fixed and re-checked, and `docs/evidence/<P1-ID>/self-review.md` (Looked at / Defects found and fixed / Remaining defects / Not covered) is committed with the images (`docs/process/visual-self-review.md`; `node art/ui/lib/live-check.mjs`). Phones and TV, full-screen and resize included.
notes: Refinement 2026-10-06 (beads checked against the code): Corrections: 'driving within ~20 s' means within ~20 s of scanning (pick a car, be on the grid or in the running race; no lobby warm-up, R110). The checklist is docs/playtests/owner-checklists.md section 3, not docs/playtests/checklist.md. The Hosts row's TCL 4K pacing run also satisfies br-iysy (native-res source and any auto-lowering named in the receipt, R111). The Party row also covers skipping the tutorial on step 1 and readying up with no prompt shown.

title: P1-R01 · Renderer foundation and backend decision
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-R01** (cites §4.3, §6.1, §10, §15.2); master cut V2-23 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D1` · **Track:** `render` · **Machine:** `on:mac` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:hardware`, `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-F03, P1-N01. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Stand up the host renderer and decide its backend with numbers: port Spike J's 24×24 bench into the host app, measure WebGPURenderer (WebGPU
and its WebGL2 backend) vs WebGLRenderer headed on the Mac's GPU, and own the host capability check so a host that can't run explains why
instead of opening a broken room. Rendering work starts before the sim worker exists by driving it from a synthetic snapshot source.

## Scope (owned paths)
`web/host/src/render/` (foundation, backend selection, synthetic snapshot source, capability check).

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Instanced vehicles (R02), map rendering (R03), grid layout (R04), cameras (R05), the in-world look (R10).

## Contract and design decisions
- Measure in **headed** browsers on the Mac (M1 Pro, the reference host that drives the TCL), and on triton's GTX 1080 or eris's RTX 2080
  SUPER as extra data points when their GPUs are clear (eris's GPU is shared with audio jobs, so check first); label the machine; never
  headless/SwiftShader numbers.
- DEFAULT rule: pick **WebGPURenderer** if it is within 15 % of WebGLRenderer and instancing + per-tile viewports work; otherwise
  **WebGLRenderer** for Playtest 1 and record why. A forced fallback path renders the same frame.
- **Host capability check** (§10, R01): before creating a room, check WebGL2 or WebGPU, WASM and module workers. If one is missing, explain why
  and offer **Join** or another device instead of opening a room it can't run (experience direction §3; master J01).
- Interpolated scene updates from snapshots, driven at first by a **synthetic snapshot source** implementing the §4.4 ABI (`Snapshot{buf,
  tick, simTime, sessionRev}`); P1-S02 swaps in the real worker. Interpolation pairs never cross a respawn.
- three r186+ stable, bundled (no CDN).

## Interfaces
- Consumes: F03 pins, N01 ABI types. Provides: renderer + synthetic source to R02, R03, R04, R09; capability check to the host landing flow (G00/C01).

## Reuses / gap
Reuses Spike J's 24×24 bench (J `REPORT.md`). Gap: no host app renderer, no backend decision.

## Required tests
- Bench table (headed Playwright on the real GPU) per backend at 1080p and 4K; forced-fallback capture equality.
- Playwright: a browser with WebGL2 and WebGPU disabled gets the capability explanation and a Join link, and no room is created.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
Bench table + captures (headed Playwright on the real GPU). Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-R01/`.

## How this bead closes
- `ev:hardware`: a perf/network receipt naming hardware, browser/backend, build and cohort, closed through the evidence close (`batch-verify.sh close <id> --evidence <file>`, P1-F02).
- `ev:ci`: green Gitea CI on a commit containing this bead, cited as `receipt:<run url>` with a `batch_verify` gate pass (before CI exists, a committed local receipt; while CI is down, the verifier's `batch-verify.sh` receipt).

## Working rules
Follow `AGENTS.md` (owner rules first) and `docs/process/bead-workflow.md`: check your own area, commit with `P1-R01` and the bead ID in the message, push, and close this bead once CI is green on a commit containing it (gate pass, ticked items, `receipt:<run url>`).

## Anti-narrowing clause
> Done only when the FELT, observable outcome above holds in the RUNNING game via the real host path. Passing unit/geometry tests is necessary but NOT sufficient.

title: P1-R02 · Instanced vehicle renderer
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-R02** (cites §6.1, §6.3, §10); master cut V2-23 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D1` · **Track:** `render` · **Machine:** `on:mac` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:hardware`, `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-R01, P1-V02. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Render every car, loose part and detached part with **one InstancedMesh per part type** so draw calls per tile stay constant in N (216 draws
for 24 cars × 24 tiles vs 3,602 naive), with per-tile LOD classes sharing one instance buffer, paint from the identity colour, and buffers
that grow without a cap.

## Scope (owned paths)
`web/host/src/render/vehicles/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Map rendering (R03), cameras (R05), identity overlays (R06), the in-world look materials (R10).

## Contract and design decisions
§6.1 rows adopted as REQUIRED/DEFAULT:
- **One InstancedMesh per part type** across all cars (REQUIRED). Reference row (Spike J `REPORT.md`): 24×24, 1080p, LOD1, instanced, culling
  off → **216 draws, 506 k tris, 3.6 ms median / 5.1 ms p90** on an M1 Pro (5.1 / 6.4 ms at 4K).
- **Paint key** (REQUIRED identity colour path): atlas texels that are pure white tint by `instanceColor`; glass/lamps/livery keep colour; one
  material for all cars.
- **LOD per tile** (DEFAULT): all cars in a tile share a LOD class (tile height ≥ 540 px LOD0, ≥ 200 px LOD1, else LOD2). One InstancedMesh per
  part type **per LOD class**, all sharing one instance-matrix/colour buffer per part type; each tile's render pass shows only its LOD class's
  meshes, so heterogeneous tiles cost no extra uploads.
- Shadow map once per frame, not per tile. Instancing per part type, not BatchedMesh (BatchedMesh flat draws hold only for one shared camera
  and conflict with per-part detach).
- Loose parts = the part's instance with the hinge rotation applied; detached parts = the same part-type instance with a physics-driven
  matrix; a missing part shows the core's dark bay; detached parts keep the owner's paint colour.
- **Growable instance buffers, no cap** (R66). Perf receipts report draws, tris and frame time.

  show QR + standings), replacing master §6.2's filler default if the owner picked another.
- Master §6.2 starting constraints: rows·cols ≥ N minimising unused area; tile aspect in a playable band (~1.2–2.0 TP, FP a little narrower);

title: P1-R06 · Identity kit and Identify
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-R06** (cites §10; master §5.1, §5.2); master cut V2-16, V2-17 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D2` · **Track:** `render` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-R02, P1-R04, P1-N07a, P1-C02, P1-C05, P1-U04. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Make "which car am I?" a one-second question (R4, R22): roof number, paint colour, nameplates over cars in other tiles, the tile badge, and
the Identify pulse visible ≤ 150 ms after the press, auto-firing on join and respawn.

## Scope (owned paths)
`web/host/src/identity/`, `web/controller/src/identity/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The seat number/colour assignment (N07a); the Identify button's placement on the controller (C02).

## Contract and design decisions
- Identity: roof number, paint colour (paint key, R02), nameplate over cars in other tiles, tile badge with number + name. Numbers are not
  capped at 99 (labels above 99 render). Colour-blind safety from number + colour (patterns are Full).
- **Identify** (master §5.2): for ~1.5 s the player's tile border and number badge pulse and scale up, a comic "#7 THAT'S YOU!" burst appears
  over their car, their car gets a bright outline visible in **other** tiles; the controller flashes the same number/colour full-screen (and
  vibrates where supported). **≤ 150 ms press-to-visible** (R4). Auto-fires once on join and on respawn. Rate-limited once per 3 s (N07a).

title: P1-R09 · Highlight recorder and reel
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-R09** (cites §10, §9; master §10.3, §10.4); master cut V2-76, V2-77 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).

**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-R02, P1-G01. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
The end-of-round highlight reel (R57: no live killcam/PIP): a memory-budgeted recorder of quantised transforms plus retained clips around
big events, played full-screen in intermission with a broadcast-style camera and identity labels, never touching live simulation.

## Scope (owned paths)
`web/host/src/reel/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Damage itself (S04*; the reel over real damage is checked in P1-Q02, journey J10).

## Contract and design decisions
- Recorder: a ring of quantised transforms (**30 Hz, ~20 s**) plus retained clips around events (detach, wreck, air > 1.2 s, close finish;
  **3 s before, 2 s after**), within a memory budget (R67, DEFAULT **64 MB**). Stored replay capacity is a permitted memory budget; it never
  limits live play.
- At round end select **~60 s**, favouring players not yet shown; play full-screen with a broadcast-style orbit camera and identity labels.
- Never touches live simulation; skipping (host Hide replay) never affects the next round; results stay visible.
- **Owner, 2026-10-03:** this bead needs no owner approval; the couch test (P1-Q02) doesn't wait for it, and it ships in the next preview
  when it lands. It styles from the current token file (draft or accepted) and the accepted results mock when one exists.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: R02 rendering, G01 events/phases. Provides: the reel in intermission to G01's loop, A03 (cues during reel), Q02 (J10).

## Required tests
- Scripted run (synthetic snapshots + events, so it doesn't wait for S04) with two detaches and a wreck → reel contains them with correct identities.
- Ring eviction keeps retained clips; memory within budget (numbers recorded).
- Skipping never affects the next round; a real two-round Playwright run plays the reel in intermission and still starts the next round on time.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence

description:

## Purpose and observable outcome
The derby's shared screen: one Overview camera framing every car big and readable on the TV, with identity rings and edge-band HUD, and a
host switch between Grid and Overview at any time. The POC already designs it (U02/U05); this builds it.

## Scope (owned paths)
`web/host/src/camera/overview/`, `web/host/src/ui/overview/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Grid layout (R04) and per-car cameras (R05); derby rules (S10).

## Contract and design decisions
Overview camera (master §6.4, R22, R23): one camera framing the action, no split. Frames the **cars' bounding box** plus margin
(never empty arena), clamped to arena bounds, fixed pitch ≈ 55–65°, never rotates, critically damped zoom; at high N it settles at "whole arena" and
stays (stability beats tightness). Every human-controlled car stays visible; never crop an outlier to hit a median-size target (a hard spread gives
a non-blocking Grid suggestion). Identity: nameplate + number + colour ring under each car, scaled by camera distance (nameplate ≥ 28 px at 4K).
HUD in thin edge bands (the 3-minute timer, damage-points standings). Host can switch Grid ⇄ Overview **at any time, including mid-round**, with
a ~300 ms animated transition; Overview only on arena maps (on track maps it's disabled with an explanation). Auto default: arena maps start in
Overview, tracks in Grid. No killcam/PIP. Built to the accepted POC Overview mock (P1-U02/U05, `art/ui/accepted/<date>/`).

## Interfaces
- Consumes: R02/R03 rendering, R04 grid, the accepted Overview mock (U04), the arena (M10). Provides: the Overview to G06 and the host controls.

  padded envelope ≤ 35 % of the frame (initial target), every car visible; record the metric mask and viewing profile.
- A spread-out case keeps every car visible (no cropping) and offers the non-blocking Grid suggestion.
- Grid ⇄ Overview switches mid-round with a ~300 ms transition; on a track map the switch is disabled with an explanation.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
Captures + metric output. Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-R11/`.

title: P1-S01 · `jj-sim` core and scenario runner
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-S01** (cites §6.1, §7.1, §7.2, §8.1, §14); master cut V2-06, V2-07 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D1` · **Track:** `sim` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-N01, P1-M01. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
The authoritative simulation core (R61): a Rapier world built from `jj.map.v1`, a raycast vehicle, seeded RNG, a full-state hash, an
applied-tick input journal and a bootstrap scenario runner, plus a Rapier 0.36 API fixture that pins the semantics every later sim bead
relies on. On the critical path (… M01 → S01 → S02 …).

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-sim/`, `crates/jj-tools/src/scenario/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The browser worker (S02), feel tuning (S03), damage (S04*), race rules (S05), placement (S06), autopilot (S07), utilities (S08); the shared introspection surface and `jj sim` (F05a turns S01's runner into it; S01 doesn't depend on F05a).

## Contract and design decisions
Time and ticks (plan §7.1): 120 Hz fixed step, `dt = 1/120` (R61). The worker owns the accumulator and steps whole ticks; rendering
interpolates between the last two snapshots. **Tick order:** apply commands and inputs due at this tick → set vehicle controls and surface
friction → `update_vehicle` against current query data → `step` → read contact data and build damage episodes → apply structural changes
(detach, spawn, respawn) → race progress → emit ordered events → publish snapshot when a buffer is free. Persistently unplayable lag
enters `performance-stall` at the last completed tick; never enlarge `dt`, skip ticks, delete debris or refuse joins.

Determinism (plan §7.2): seeded RNG streams, stable iteration order, no wall clock in the sim, Rapier `enhanced-determinism`. Same-build
same-target runs produce identical full-state hashes. Native vs WASM physics identity is a **measured** claim checked where the fixtures live
(S01 runner, S02 worker, S03 feel bank): target identical full-state hashes; if they differ, record where they diverge and compare feel
scenarios by envelopes and discrete events (detach, lap, finish) instead, and say so in the receipt. Canonical **map bytes** must match
native vs WASM exactly, always.

Rapier footguns to re-verify on Rust 0.36 (plan §6.1, Spike C used the JS API): `update_vehicle` doesn't wake a sleeping chassis;
brake is an impulse per tick, engine force is a force; external forces fight the wheel-slip model. Engineering rule (AGENTS.md): use
Rapier's vehicle controller as documented for the pinned version; never multiply/divide by large factors "to make it work"; sustained
forces integrate with `dt` once; impulses apply once. Document findings in code and `docs/learnings/sim.md`.

- Rapier world from `jj.map.v1`: heightfield, barriers, dressing colliders from the **kit registry's collider proxies** (§8.1, `assets/kit/`).
- Raycast vehicle from a vehicle profile: a **provisional profile with Spike J's Cruze dimensions** until P1-V02's sidecar exists (P1-S03
  switches to the sidecar).
- Seeded RNG streams; full-state hash; **applied-tick input journal** (the one sim funnel: phones, pads, keys, autopilot, test bots and
  replays all enter as applied-tick inputs; nothing changes sim state except journaled setup commands).
- Bootstrap scenario file format + runner (JSON fixtures under `scenarios/`; outcome signatures).
- **Static determinism scan** re-expressed from 0.1 (`static/js/engine/determinism.js`, `tests/unit/determinism-static-scan.test.js`): a Rust
  lint/test forbidding wall clock / unseeded random in sim code.
- The crate passes `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: N01 types; M01 map loader + kit registry; Spike J dimensions (provisional profile).
- Provides: the sim core to S02 (worker), F05a (surface), S03–S08; the journal format F07 replays; Rapier API notes for S04b (wheel disable).

## Reuses / gap
Reuses Spike C's Rapier findings and Spike J's Cruze dimensions; gap: no Rust sim, no journal/hash, no scenario runner.

## Required tests
- Scenario bank: `idle-settle` and `straight-throttle` (native).
- Determinism: same inputs + seed → same hash across two runs; journal replay reproduces the hash.
- Rapier 0.36 API fixture: `update_vehicle` against the query pipeline before `step`; brake vs engine-force units; a sleeping chassis waking
  on control input; per-wheel state access; how to disable one wheel.
- The static determinism scan (fails on an injected `SystemTime::now()`/unseeded RNG in sim code).

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
Scenario output + hashes. Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-S01/`.

## How this bead closes

title: P1-S02 · Sim worker (WASM) and lifecycle
description:

## Purpose and observable outcome
Run `jj-session` + `jj-input` + `jj-sim` as WASM in a host Web Worker that owns the 120 Hz clock, decodes controller bytes itself, publishes
pooled snapshots and ordered events, and pauses/resumes correctly when the host tab hides. Rendering rate never changes the simulation.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-wasm-host/`, `web/host/src/worker/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Rendering (R01/R02), host pads/keys sampling (C05), test messages (F05b), map preparation flow wiring (G01, M08a).

## Contract and design decisions
Time and ticks (plan §7.1): 120 Hz fixed step, `dt = 1/120` (R61). The worker owns the accumulator and steps whole ticks; rendering
interpolates between the last two snapshots. **Tick order:** apply commands and inputs due at this tick → set vehicle controls and surface
friction → `update_vehicle` against current query data → `step` → read contact data and build damage episodes → apply structural changes
(detach, spawn, respawn) → race progress → emit ordered events → publish snapshot when a buffer is free. Persistently unplayable lag
enters `performance-stall` at the last completed tick; never enlarge `dt`, skip ticks, delete debris or refuse joins.

Worker ABI (plan §4.4; see P1-N01 for the full table): main → sim `Init`, `NetBytes`, `LocalSource`, `Ui`, `Lifecycle`, `MapReady`,
`ReturnBuffer`; sim → main `Snapshot` (transferable), `Events` (ordered), `Journal`, `Outbound`.
- Controller bytes are decoded by `jj-protocol` and interpreted by `jj-input` **inside the worker**, the same path as `LocalSource`.
- Worker-owned 120 Hz scheduler; **pooled transferable snapshots** (bulk binary, no per-entity calls); if no pooled buffer is free the worker
  skips that publish and never blocks physics or drops events.
- **Pause reasons** compose: `manual`, `host-hidden`, `renderer-unavailable`, `performance-stall`, `fault`. Hidden time is never replayed;
  resume goes through a short visible countdown with input re-armed at neutral. Controller loss never pauses (R45).
- Interpolation pairs come from the same round/life (never interpolate across a respawn).
- A worker panic / unrecoverable WASM error = the `fault` pause reason (the host shows "Something broke" with Save bug clip / New room; R84).
Determinism (plan §7.2): seeded RNG streams, stable iteration order, no wall clock in the sim, Rapier `enhanced-determinism`. Same-build
same-target runs produce identical full-state hashes. Native vs WASM physics identity is a **measured** claim checked where the fixtures live
(S01 runner, S02 worker, S03 feel bank): target identical full-state hashes; if they differ, record where they diverge and compare feel
scenarios by envelopes and discrete events (detach, lap, finish) instead, and say so in the receipt. Canonical **map bytes** must match
native vs WASM exactly, always.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: S01 core, N06 input, N07a seats.
- Provides: the worker to F05b, R01 (replaces the synthetic snapshot source), C05, G00→G04, S03 (WASM parity through `jj-wasm-host` in Node).

- hiding the tab pauses with no catch-up; resume shows a countdown with neutral re-arm;
- starving snapshot buffers never blocks physics.

A drivable, fun-first Cruz Missile: the §7.3 behaviours as scenario-bank cases with outcome signatures, the S03-owned affordance rows, the
authority metric and `jj sim --sweep` for tuning, built from the baked V02 sidecar. This is the baseline the owner drives first in G04's free

## Contract and design decisions
Vehicle feel (plan §7.3; targets are TUNE, judged at G-FEEL):
| Affordance | DEFAULT starting behaviour | Scenario |
|---|---|---|
| Suspension | Soft springs, strong damping, visible roll/squat/dive, single-settle landings | `idle-settle`, `jump-land` |
| Steer/throttle/brake/reverse | DRIVE X steers; up throttles; down brakes, reversing near rest | `progressive-brake`, `slalom` |
| Handbrake drift | ACTION left: rear friction slip × 0.35, 0.4 s smooth recovery; drifting charges boost | `drift-entry-exit` |
| Boost | ACTION right: meter 0–1, drains 0.35/s, recharges 0.12/s, +60 % engine force | `boost-hold` |
| Wheelie ("lift and launch", R64) | DRIVE pulled past full brake (y < −0.85) preloads; release = leaving the preload zone and passing y > −0.3 within 250 ms; lift scales with preload time (max at 0.4 s); held past 1.2 s cancels; needs ≥ 3 wheels grounded. Payoff (DEFAULT, TUNE): well-timed release (preload 0.35–1.2 s) adds +15 % drive force for 0.8 s and lifts the front enough to hop kerb-height obstacles and small debris; an early release only lifts a little; a late one does nothing; steering reduced while the front is up | `wheelie-ok`, `wheelie-fail`, `brake-no-wheelie` |
| Air control | Mild pitch/roll torque from DRIVE while airborne | `air-level` |
| Surfaces | Per surface ID friction multipliers: tarmac 1.0, packed dirt 0.8, gravel 0.7, rock 0.9 | `surface-deltas` |

Affordance bank (plan §7.3a): each row is a scenario-bank case in `scenarios/affordances/` with an outcome signature, run from several
starting states and compared with mash, hold and no-input baselines. Numbers are TUNE envelopes set at the first accepted playtest.
Each row also gets the §13b.1 four-step check when its tuning changes: (1) replay to show determinism; (2) change one input timing or
parameter to show agency and a causal difference; (3) debug-only ablations and solver stress (more substeps/iterations, high speed) to reject
numerical accidents; (4) the owner playtests. Mash and no-input baselines must differ from deliberate driving.

S03-owned affordance rows:
| The player can… | Scenario |
|---|---|
| Go forward and backward from rest, on every surface, without an accidental wheelie or stunt | `fwd-back-rest` |
| Stop: progressive braking reaches a stop within an envelope from 10/20/30 m/s | `brake-stop` |
| Turn around inside the road width (three-point turn) | `turn-around` |
| Reverse out of a nose-in wall or barrier contact within 2 s | `unstick-wall` |
| Steer with authority at 5/15/30 m/s and counter-steer out of a slide | `authority`, `slalom` |
| Enter and leave a drift on purpose, and gain boost from it | `drift-entry-exit` |
| Go meaningfully faster with boost than without, and boost-forever isn't the best line | `boost-line` |
| Wheelie only from the pull-release gesture, never from braking | `wheelie-ok`, `brake-no-wheelie` |
| Level the car in the air and land a jump on its wheels | `air-level`, `jump-land` (M03d shares) |
| Get back onto the route from the verge or a ditch | `rejoin-route` |

**Authority metric** (re-expressed from 0.1 `static/js/systems/steeringAuthority.js`, `tests/unit/steering-authority.test.js`): heading change
from full steer in 0.5 s at 5/15/30 m/s. `jj sim --sweep PARAM=A..B` over profile parameters → CSV (S03 adds the flag to F05a's `jj sim`).
Every scenario carries an outcome signature; each tuning change follows the §13b.1 four-step check. Owner feel verdicts from G04 (round
records) are inputs, never gates.

Reuses S01's runner/scenario format and F05a's surface; 0.1's authority metric idea. Gap: no tuned, measured vehicle feel.

title: P1-S04 · Damage: loose, detach, debris, wreck (epic)
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-S04** (cites §6.3, §7.3a, §13b.1); master cut V2-60/62/63 slice, R86 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D3` · **Track:** `sim` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-S03, P1-V03. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Epic for R86 damage in Playtest 1: parts go intact → loose → detached, debris persists dynamically for the round, wrecks respawn in ~2 s.
Split along master §18.4's order: episode attribution → part damage (S04a) → safe hinge/detach/mass update (S04b) → wrecks and
persistent-body qualification (S04c). Consumers (G05, Q01) depend on this epic, i.e. on all three children.

## Scope (owned paths)
Children own `crates/jj-sim/src/damage/` and `scenarios/damage/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Rendering of loose/detached parts (R02 supports it from synthetic snapshots; V03 provides dark bays and hinge data).

## Contract and design decisions
Damage model (plan §6.3, R86): each part goes **intact → loose → detached**. No dents.
- **Health** (DEFAULT/TUNE): `front` 100, `back` 100, each door 60, each wheel 80.
- **Damage episodes:** every part is its own collider on the chassis body, so a contact's collider handle names the part. Per (car, part,
  other body), aggregate normal impulses over a **50 ms** game-time window; count only contacts with closing speed **≥ 4 m/s** (TUNE),
  excluding resting and suspension support. Damage = `k_part × Σ impulse`. Calibrate `k` with scenarios, not formulas:
  | Scenario | Expected |
  |---|---|
  | `bump-4`: 4 m/s nudge into another car | no damage |
  | `rest-60`: parked against a wall for 60 s | no damage |
  | `side-swipe-8`: 8 m/s door-to-door | that door goes loose, nothing detaches |
  | `wall-head-on-15`: 15 m/s into a wall | `front` detaches |
  | `t-bone-12`: 12 m/s into a door | that door detaches |
  | `wheel-kerb-12`: 12 m/s wheel strike on a barrier end | that wheel goes loose |
- **Wheel colliders:** small cylinders/balls at each hub, in a collision group that **excludes terrain and road**, so wheel strikes from
  cars/debris/barriers register without fighting the raycast suspension.
- **Loose** (health ≤ 50 %): the part stays attached and its collider stays at the attached pose. `jj-sim` integrates a damped 1-DOF spring
  about the part's hinge axis, driven by chassis acceleration (deterministic, in snapshots, replayable). Limits: doors 0–70° about the front
  edge; bumpers hang 0–25° about their top edge; wheels wobble ±6° camber. A loose wheel loses 15 % friction slip (TUNE). Visual springs, not
  joints (joints risk injecting energy, Spike I).
- **Detached** (health 0): at the end of the tick remove the part's collider from the chassis, create a dynamic body with the part's proxy
  and mass at its current world pose, set velocity to the chassis velocity at that point (`v + ω × r`) plus a small outward kick, recompute
  chassis mass properties. A detached wheel disables that wheel in the vehicle controller (zero suspension force, friction and engine
  force; verify the Rapier 0.36 API) so that corner drops onto its collider.
- **Debris persists** for the round as dynamic bodies that may sleep and wake (R58, R66): no TTL, cap, static conversion or merging.
- **Wreck:** ≥ 2 wheels detached, or stuck/flipped past the recovery timeout, or out of bounds. Remaining parts pop off as debris and the
  **husk stays as a dynamic body** (DEFAULT, Q-A2). After ~2 s (R20) the player respawns at their own legal recovery anchor in a fresh
  intact car with the same identity and progress.
- **Rendering:** loose = the part's instance with the hinge rotation applied; detached = the same part-type instance with a physics-driven
  matrix; a missing part shows the core's dark bay; detached parts keep the owner's paint colour.

## Interfaces
- Children inherit this epic's external deps (S03, V03). Provides damage state in snapshots/events to R02, R09, G05, A03.

title: P1-S04a · Contact episodes and part health
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-S04a** (cites §6.3, §7.3a); master cut V2-60 slice (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).

**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-S03, P1-V03, P1-F05a. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Attribute every hit to the right part and turn it into health loss, calibrated by scenarios so a nudge or resting contact does nothing and
real crashes do the expected damage. State is introspectable before any detach physics exists.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-sim/src/damage/episodes.rs` (or similar), `scenarios/damage/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Loose springs, detach and debris (S04b); wrecks/respawn (S04c).

## Contract and design decisions
Damage model (plan §6.3, R86): each part goes **intact → loose → detached**. No dents.
- **Health** (DEFAULT/TUNE): `front` 100, `back` 100, each door 60, each wheel 80.
- **Damage episodes:** every part is its own collider on the chassis body, so a contact's collider handle names the part. Per (car, part,
  other body), aggregate normal impulses over a **50 ms** game-time window; count only contacts with closing speed **≥ 4 m/s** (TUNE),
  excluding resting and suspension support. Damage = `k_part × Σ impulse`. Calibrate `k` with scenarios, not formulas:
  | Scenario | Expected |
  |---|---|
  | `bump-4`: 4 m/s nudge into another car | no damage |
  | `rest-60`: parked against a wall for 60 s | no damage |
  | `side-swipe-8`: 8 m/s door-to-door | that door goes loose, nothing detaches |
  | `wall-head-on-15`: 15 m/s into a wall | `front` detaches |
  | `t-bone-12`: 12 m/s into a door | that door detaches |
  | `wheel-kerb-12`: 12 m/s wheel strike on a barrier end | that wheel goes loose |
- **Wheel colliders:** small cylinders/balls at each hub, in a collision group that **excludes terrain and road**, so wheel strikes from
  cars/debris/barriers register without fighting the raycast suspension.

The §7.3a row `control-after-hit`: regain control within ~1 s after a side hit or a T-bone that doesn't wreck the car.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: S03 profile/car, V03 production part colliders, F05a surface. Provides: part health/state (introspected + in snapshots) to S04b.

Reuses S03's feel bank cars and F05a fixtures. Gap: no part attribution or health.

title: P1-S04b · Loose springs, detach and persistent debris
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-S04b** (cites §6.3, §13b.1); master cut V2-62 slice (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).

## Purpose and observable outcome
Make damage visible and physical: loose parts swing on deterministic springs, detached parts become dynamic debris with inherited velocity,
mass updates are exact, and nothing ever deletes, merges, freezes or budgets debris. Energy accounting proves the springs and kicks don't
inject energy.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-sim/src/damage/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Wrecks/husks/respawn (S04c). Rendering (R02/V03).

## Contract and design decisions
- Hinge springs: damped 1-DOF about each part's hinge axis, driven by chassis acceleration; deterministic; published in snapshots; limits
  doors 0–70° about the front edge, bumpers 0–25° about their top edge, wheels ±6° camber; a loose wheel loses 15 % friction slip (TUNE).
- Detach at the end of the tick with `v + ω × r` + a small outward kick; chassis mass recompute; detached-wheel disable in the vehicle
  controller (verify the Rapier 0.36 API; S01's fixture pins how).
- Debris persists for the round as dynamic bodies that may sleep and wake: **no static conversion, deletion, merging or count budget
  anywhere** (R58, R66).
- **Energy accounting** (§13b.1): `Δ(kinetic + potential) − authorised work` stays under a solver-calibrated tolerance; a positive residual
  is a bug candidate.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: S04a part states. Provides: detach events + debris bodies to S04c, S09 (detached door for the hop duel), R02/R09/G05.

## Reuses / gap
Reuses Spike C (detach → dynamic debris in Rapier works: velocity + angular transfer, mass removed, sleeps, wakes on contact) and Spike I (springs not joints). Gap: none of it exists in Rust.

## Required tests
- Scenario bank: detached parts inherit velocity, stay dynamic, sleep and wake on contact at round end; mass totals before/after.
- A grep + test proving no static conversion, deletion, merging or count budget.
- Energy accounting for loose springs, detach kicks and a 20-part debris pile, including a solver-stress rerun with doubled substeps.
- §7.3a `loose-wheel-drive`.

title: P1-S05 · Race rules and recovery
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-S05** (cites §7.4, §7.5, §14); master cut V2-73a, V2-102 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D1` · **Track:** `sim` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-S01, P1-M01, P1-F05a. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Legal progress, recovery and race completion in the sim: gates in order, anchors, flip assist, Recover, out-of-bounds, laps, the finish
window, the absolute deadline and finished-car ghosting. "Out of bounds always recovers" is a 0.1 lesson kept.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-sim/src/race/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Placement and drop-in (S06), autopilot (S07), results/points (N07c), wreck mechanics (S04c).

## Contract and design decisions
Recovery and race rules (plan §7.4–§7.5):
- **Flip assist** (load-bearing, Spike C: a rounded cabin doesn't self-right at these proportions): when up·Y < 0.2 and speed < 2 m/s for
  1 s, apply a visible self-right torque; if still inverted 3 s after the assist starts (4 s after coming to rest inverted), the car is wrecked.
- **Recover** button: available when speed < 3 m/s for 1 s or inverted; 2 s penalty; respawn at the own anchor.
- **Out of bounds:** below the kill height or outside map bounds → wreck → respawn.
- **Route** = the map's centerline with checkpoint gates (~every 40 m). Legal progress needs gates in order; the **recovery anchor** is the last
  gate passed, offset onto the centerline at a clear pose. Never use raw nearest-spline projection at crossings/shortcuts.
- **Race end:** 3 laps DEFAULT; a 30 s window after the first finisher; absolute deadline `max(180 s, 2 × laps × refLap)` from countdown
  completion; finished cars stop colliding with racers (and debris) and coast on autopilot (keep terrain collision and their tile);
  unfinished cars rank by legal progress (master §10.12).

Re-express from 0.1 (§14): `tests/e2e/oob-recovery.spec.ts` (out-of-bounds always recovers) as a Rust scenario.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: S01, M01 (route, gates, bounds), F05a. Provides: progress/anchors to S06, S07, N07c, R07 (HUD lap/position), G01 (JN2).

## Required tests
Scenario bank `crates/jj-sim/tests/race.rs`: OOB always recovers; a flip from 12 inverted poses rights itself or is wrecked within 4 s of
coming to rest; a shortcut across the infield doesn't count progress; the first finisher starts the window; an all-stuck race ends at the
deadline; §7.3a `flip-recover`, `oob-recover`.

title: P1-S06 · Placement service and drop-in
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-S06** (cites §7.5, §14; master §6.5, §10.9); master cut V2-18, V2-123 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D1` · **Track:** `sim` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-S05. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
One placement service for start grids, respawns and drop-in that works for any N with no cap, queue or refusal: the old 0.1 silent spawn cap
must never return. Late joiners land ~3 s behind the last racer with that car's lap/gate state.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-sim/src/placement/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Wreck triggers (S04c), the browser-side drop-in journey (G02).

## Contract and design decisions
Placement service (plan §7.5; one service for start grid, respawn and drop-in): commit placements at tick boundaries against current cars and
debris; **1.5 s spawn protection** disables car/debris contacts (terrain and barriers stay solid) and only ends in a non-overlapping pose.
**Start grid for any N without a cap or queue:** rows fill the map's declared start corridor back along the route; once the corridor is full,
further cars are placed in it anyway under spawn protection (ghosted against cars and debris) and turn solid only when clear. Nobody waits,
is refused or is dropped. **Drop-in (R63):** a new seat spawns ~3 s of route behind the last still-racing car, with that car's lap/gate state,

title: P1-S09 · Skill-payoff duels
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-S09** (cites §7.3b, §13b.1); master cut V2-40/V2-41a part, owner 2026-10-02 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D3` · **Track:** `sim` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-S03, P1-S04b. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Prove that doing techniques **well pays off, badly costs, and none dominates** (owner: "the drifting player around a corner beats the
normal player"; "the forward/back wheelie beats players when executed perfectly vs not"). Mash never wins.

## Scope (owned paths)
`scenarios/duels/`, `crates/jj-sim/src/vehicle/` (tuning only), `assets/profiles/cruz-missile.json`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The drivable baseline (S03); the cone-defence duel (S08). L-plates reuse these duels later (Full, R64).

## Contract and design decisions
Each duel runs identical cars on the same greybox segment from the same state with scripted inputs: a **plain** line, a **well-executed**
technique (timing found by `jj sim --sweep`, then frozen in the fixture) and a **botched** one (too early, too late or held too long). The
assertion is an ordering on time to a gate after the segment, with TUNE margins.
| Duel | Expect |
|---|---|
| `drift-corner-duel` (hairpin at 18 m/s entry) | well-timed drift + its banked boost beats brake-and-steer; a mistimed drift loses or spins |
| `drift-boost-chain` (S-bend then straight) | drifting both bends and spending the boost on the straight beats a grip driver over the sector |
| `drift-straight-penalty` | drifting down a straight is slower than driving it straight |
| `wheelie-launch-duel` (from 0 and from 8 m/s) | a well-timed pull-release launch beats plain full throttle to a gate 40 m on; early release no better than plain; late/held worse |
| `wheelie-hop-duel` (a kerb or a detached door across the line) | the hop clears it and keeps speed; plain driving hits it and loses speed |
| `boost-placement-duel` | the same boost spent on the straight beats it spent into a corner |
| `air-control-duel` (greybox jump) | levelling lands on its wheels and keeps speed; no input lands nose-first and loses more; over-correcting is worst |
| `mash-duel` | in each duel above, a mash script never beats the well-executed line |
Every tuning change follows the §13b.1 four-step check and must keep every S03 and S04 affordance row passing. The owner's G04 feel notes
(round records) are inputs; margins are decided by the owner's feel verdict at playtests.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: S03 feel bank + sweep; S04b (detached door). Provides: tuned profile to G04+ and the duel table to Q02.

## Reuses / gap
Reuses S03's feel bank, fixtures and sweep; fills the "doing it well pays off" gap. Depends on S04b because the wheelie-hop duel needs a detached door.

## Required tests
- Scenario bank `scenarios/duels/` replayed natively and through WASM; the sweep CSVs used to freeze timings committed as evidence.

title: P1-S10 · Derby rules and damage-point scoring
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-S10** (cites master §10.9, §10.12; R56; owner 2026-10-03); master cut V2-105 + V2-126 derby slice (owner 2026-10-03) (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D6` · **Track:** `sim` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-S04, P1-S06, P1-N07c, P1-M10. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
The derby game rules in the sim and session: a 3-minute round won on damage dealt to opponents, with honest attribution so self-wrecks, spawn
protection and the environment never score, fast respawn, and late joiners welcome.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-sim/src/derby/` (attribution, round clock), `crates/jj-session/src/results/` (derby classification), `scenarios/derby/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The arena (P1-M10); the Overview camera (P1-R11); round-loop wiring and the lobby mode choice (P1-G06); last-man-standing (P1-S11).

## Contract and design decisions
Owner direction 2026-10-03: the first derby is **passive containment** (the bowl's walls and lip keep cars in; **no shrinking
wall** or other arena-closing mechanism) and is **won on damage dealt** (R56: a 3-minute round ranked by raw damage points; late joiners are
allowed and simply have less time). A **last-man-standing** mode comes later (P1-S11, deferred) with a host switch for drop-in while playing.

Derby raw points (master §10.12): each accepted HP of opponent damage gives 1 point, a detach gives +5 and a wreck +20, once per
part/life event. Self, friendly-fire, spawn-protected and environmental damage give zero. Integer damage units of 0.001 HP and score units of
1/2000 point: normal damage earns twice its damage units; bonuses are exact integers. Autopilot halves the credited event once, so a 10 HP +
detach + wreck episode gives 35 human points or 17.5 autopilot points. The sim records control mode at the causal action, not at display time.
Secondary debris attribution expires 3 s game time after the last qualifying instigator impulse; after that it's environmental. Equal raw scores
share rank; championship conversion uses the same table as Race (`[25,18,15,12,10,8,6,4,2,1]`, then 1 for every later rank) with no finish bonus.
Combo callouts are presentation only (no multiplier).

- Round: 3 minutes on game time (paused with game time), ranked by raw points; equal raw scores share rank.
- Respawn after a wreck in ~2 s at a safe edge pose through the placement service (arena policy), with spawn protection (no damage dealt or
  taken while protected).
- Late joiners (R56): allowed at any time, spawn at a safe edge pose, score from when they arrive; no normalisation.
- Damage itself comes from the S04 model (intact → loose → detached, husks stay, debris stays dynamic); S10 only attributes and scores it.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: S04 damage episodes, S06 placement, N07c results. Provides: derby facts (points, events) in snapshots/events to R11's HUD bands, G06, A03 cues.

## Reuses / gap
Reuses S04's contact episodes (adds the instigator to each) and N07c's classification. Gap: no attribution or derby scoring.

## Required tests
- Fixture: the master example: a 10 HP + detach + wreck episode scores 35 human points and 17.5 autopilot points.
- Fixtures: self-damage, spawn-protected and environmental damage score zero; debris attribution expires after 3 s; equal raw scores share rank.
- A late joiner's ranking uses raw points; the 3-minute clock pauses with game time.

## Purpose and observable outcome
A second derby mode: wrecked cars are out (no respawn) and the last car running wins, with a host switch for whether new players may drop in

  the owner wants that).
- **"Drop in while playing" switch** (host setting, next-round effect): **on** → a new player enters the running round at a safe edge pose like
  any derby late joiner; **off** → a new player joins the room at once, gets their seat, number and colour, and enters at the next round. "Off" is
  a mode rule, never a cap: nobody is refused, queued for capacity or limited in number (R36, R66).
- Scoring and results reuse S10's attribution.

title: P1-S12 · Filler bots for small groups
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-S12** (cites master §10.12 (Teams and fillers); R45); master cut V2-42 + V2-75 fillers slice (owner 2026-10-03) (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D8` · **Track:** `sim` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-S07, P1-S10, P1-G06, P1-W01. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
So two or three people still get a lively race or derby: the host can fill the field with visibly marked bots that drive, ram and use items.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-sim/src/bots/`, `crates/jj-session/src/director/` (filler target), `web/host/src/ui/` (setting + bot badge).

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Dropout autopilot (S07), which stays weak and only drives for absent players.

## Contract and design decisions
- Host setting **"Fill to N with bots"** (next-round effect, default off): `max(0, N − humans)` bot entrants at preparation. It's a filler
  target, never an admission limit: human joins never wait for bots, and excess bots leave at the next round boundary, never by deleting a
  racing car or its debris (master §10.12).
- Bots are visibly marked, have no ballot or Ready, never count towards the start condition, and appear in round results with separate bot
  standings (human event points are computed among humans).
- Driving: race bots follow the route with a skill setting (low/medium); derby bots seek and ram nearby cars and back off when stuck; bots use
  held items with simple rules (boomerang at a car in front or behind, sanga when about to be rammed). Same physics and inputs as humans.

## Required tests
- Scenarios: a 1-human + 5-bot race finishes with bots spread across the field; a derby with bots scores; a human joining mid-round never waits; bots leave at the next boundary when humans fill the field.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
Scenario + journey output. Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-S12/`.

## How this bead closes
- `ev:ci`: green Gitea CI on a commit containing this bead, cited as `receipt:<run url>` with a `batch_verify` gate pass (before CI exists, a committed local receipt; while CI is down, the verifier's `batch-verify.sh` receipt).

## Working rules
Follow `AGENTS.md` (owner rules first) and `docs/process/bead-workflow.md`: check your own area, commit with `P1-S12` and the bead ID in the message, push, and close this bead once CI is green on a commit containing it (gate pass, ticked items, `receipt:<run url>`).

## Anti-narrowing clause
> Done only when the FELT, observable outcome above holds in the RUNNING game via the real host path. Passing unit/geometry tests is necessary but NOT sufficient.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] [ev:ci] With fill-to-6 and one human, five marked bots race and finish spread across the field; in derby they ram and score.
- [ ] [ev:ci] A human joining never waits for bots, and excess bots leave at the next round boundary without deleting cars or debris.
- [ ] [ev:ci] Bots use held items with their simple rules, never count towards Ready or the start condition, and have separate standings.
- [ ] [ev:ci] Journey: the host sets Fill-to-6 in Settings with one human; marked bots appear on the grid and in separate results standings; a second controller joining never waits.
notes: Refinement 2026-10-06 (beads checked against the code): Scope adds crates/jj-session/src/results/ (separate bot standings). The Fill-to-N setting is reached from Settings (R97), not a tile overlay.

title: P1-U01 · Design guide and tokens
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-U01** (cites §3a, §13b.4; experience direction §2–§3); master cut new (owner 2026-10-02); master §12.1, §12.6 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `POC` · **Track:** `design` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** none; can start immediately.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Settle the visual language every UI task builds from, before any UI code exists (G-DESIGN, owner ruling 2026-10-02). The
output is a design guide plus **tokens as data** (`tokens.json` + schema), brand files, a component sheet, identity-under-stress
checks, a copy voice and at least three H4-style frames. C01 and D05 start from the *draft* tokens immediately; every other UI
task (C02–C04, C06, C07, R04, R06–R10) waits for the owner's verdict at P1-U04 and then builds against the accepted copy in
`art/ui/accepted/<date>/`. Observable outcome: an agent can render any UI element from `tokens.json` alone, and every listed
check passes as a scripted run.

## Scope (owned paths)
`art/ui/GUIDE.md`, `art/ui/tokens.json` (+ its JSON schema), `art/ui/fonts/`, `art/ui/frames/` (style frames and their prompts), `art/style/MASTER_PROMPTS.md` (UI block and the supersession note).

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
TV mocks (P1-U02), phone mocks (P1-U03), the in-world look and motion reel (P1-U05), the gallery and verdict (P1-U04). Turning tokens into CSS variables and shared components is P1-C01. No game code.

## Contract and design decisions
Style references (owner, 2026-10-02): **most authoritative** is the H4 round-highlights image
`docs/plans/ux-study-2026-09-29/images/H4-host-round-results-v2.png` (ink-and-cream comic panels, bold condensed headings,
yellow and cobalt accents, a painted outback world behind the chrome). The ute with the bullbar (H1, M1) shows where the
roster goes; a ute in a style frame isn't a defect. Brand badges that image generation adds (M1's grille) are placeholders
and never ship (`art/style/MASTER_PROMPTS.md` guards). **Superseded:** the drivers'-heads-out cartoony look
(`art/style/refs/ui_lobby.png`). In-game tiles in the mocks show the real Cruz Missile (Spike J,
`spikes/art-pipeline/J-cruze-lowpoly/`) because that's what Playtest 1 renders.

**Tokens as data** (`art/ui/tokens.json`, validated by a JSON schema committed beside it):
- palette with hex values and **named contrast pairs** (text/background) that the check script reads;
- an **identity palette** giving every seat a distinct colour + number for any N: numbers carry identity past the palette;
  colours are reused with distinct numbers as N grows (no cap, R66). Patterns are Full (plan §2.3), so colour + number must hold;
- two **self-hosted OFL fonts** (a condensed display face and a body face) with licence files and subsets; stable/tabular digits
  for scores, positions and countdowns (experience direction §2); no remote font service (R70);
- a **type scale per viewing profile** (TV at 3 m, desk, handheld), spacing scale, a **minimum touch target**, a **TV-safe margin**;
- ink-outline weight and the **panel wobble** spec (master §12.1: a few px at TV scale, consistent per element, never animated,
  text and hit boxes stay straight);
- icons; **motion durations** and their reduced-motion variants (U05 builds the reel from these).

**Guide** (`GUIDE.md`): the identity kit (number badge, colour, name, tile badge, Identify pulse; master §5.1–§5.2) and how the
UI chrome frames the 3D world (the in-world look itself is U05). It names a reference image for each element.

**Brand:** one wordmark (SVG), an app icon and favicon, and the **QR rule**: a plain high-contrast code with its full quiet zone
and nothing in the middle (H2's kangaroo hurts scanning), with the room code beside it in the display face.

**Components:** a sheet of every component in every state: primary, secondary and destructive buttons, panels, badges, toasts,
confirmations, progress/loading, error, disabled, and **focus for keyboard and gamepad** (experience direction §3: focus styles,
screen-reader labels and keyboard/gamepad selection are real states, not polish).

**Identity under stress:** the identity palette checked under colour-vision-deficiency simulation (protanopia, deuteranopia,
tritanopia), with numbers carrying identity wherever colours collide; 3-digit numbers; 32-grapheme names (master §10.6 limit);
non-Latin names (font coverage and a named fallback).

**Copy voice:** a short UI copy guide and glossary: one word each for room, game, seat and car; Australian spelling; button verbs;
tone consistent with P1-A00's announcer copy (`docs/copy/australianisms.md` once it exists).

**Controller in a dim room:** base colour and brightness chosen for a dark living room (DEFAULT: ink/navy base, cream panels,
the player's colour; §3a).

**Style frames:** at least three in the H4 style (the TV in-race grid with HUD, the lobby at 32, the phone controller), made
through the art pipeline (MASTER_PROMPTS + the UI block, via `codex exec`; omit `--model`), prompts committed, generated vehicles
and badges marked as placeholders. Mark `art/style/refs/ui_lobby.png` superseded in MASTER_PROMPTS.

§3a starting proposals (DEFAULT; the POC designs and shows each as ONE worked proposal with a one-line why; owner
2026-10-03: "don't give me choices on things that are obvious"; alternatives stay in evidence folders, not the gallery):
- Lobby: the warm-up drive behind the QR and player strip (plan §9).
- Grids with a gap: balanced rows first; the last row is centred and its tiles grow wider within the aspect band, so gameplay
  area comes first (master §6.2); any cell still left over shows the join QR and live standings, never black.
- Cameras: third person by default, first person per seat from the controller (master §6.3); mocks show a mixed grid.
- In-world look: master §12.1's comic treatment (faceted cars, 2–3 tone toon ramp, ink outlines, halftone in shadows); if its
  cost at 24 tiles is too high, present the cheapest version that keeps the look (e.g. outlines on cars and debris only) and say why.
- Controller in a dark room: ink/navy base with cream panels and the player's colour; the TV keeps H4's cream panels.
- Lobby at 32 and beyond: compact roster cards (number badge, colour, name, Ready) that reflow into more columns down to the
  guide's legible minimum, then compact to number + name chips. Never a "max players".

## Interfaces
- Provides: `art/ui/tokens.json` (draft) → P1-C01 (CSS variables + `web/shared/ui/`), P1-D05 (index styling), P1-U02/U03/U05
  (mocks built from tokens); later the accepted copy in `art/ui/accepted/<date>/` (P1-U04) for every UI task.
- Provides: the guide's minimum cap height / touch target / TV-safe margin, which U02/U03/R07/C02 measure against.

## Required tests
- A scripted token check (any small script under `art/ui/`, run in the wave): schema validation of `tokens.json`; WCAG AA
  contrast for every named text/background pair at its intended size; it exits non-zero naming the failing pair.
- A CVD simulation sheet generated from the identity palette (protanopia/deuteranopia/tritanopia) showing every pair of
  adjacent seats told apart by colour or number.
- A font render check of the stress names (3-digit numbers, 32 graphemes, non-Latin) with the bundled fonts or the named fallback.
- Fresh-eyes review note (§13b.4) by a reviewer that isn't the implementer: images opened at gameplay size, H4 as the named
  reference, elements present/absent, first-look reading, defects.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
Guide + tokens + component sheet + CVD sheet + frames + check output + review note. Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-U01/`.

## How this bead closes
- `ev:ci`: green Gitea CI on a commit containing this bead, cited as `receipt:<run url>` with a `batch_verify` gate pass (before CI exists, a committed local receipt; while CI is down, the verifier's `batch-verify.sh` receipt).

## Working rules
Follow `AGENTS.md` (owner rules first) and `docs/process/bead-workflow.md`: check your own area, commit with `P1-U01` and the bead ID in the message, push, and close this bead once CI is green on a commit containing it (gate pass, ticked items, `receipt:<run url>`).

## Anti-narrowing clause
> Done only when the FELT, observable outcome above holds in the RUNNING game via the real host path. Passing unit/geometry tests is necessary but NOT sufficient.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] [ev:ci] `tokens.json` validates against its committed schema (scripted check).
- [x] [ev:ci] Every text/background pair `tokens.json` names passes WCAG AA at its intended size (scripted check output).
- [x] [ev:ci] The identity palette's CVD simulation sheet (protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia) shows every pair of adjacent seats told apart by colour or number.
- [x] [ev:ci] The two display/body fonts are local OFL files with licences and subsets, and they (or the named fallback) render the stress names: 3-digit numbers, 32-grapheme names, non-Latin names.
- [x] [ev:ci] The wordmark (SVG), app icon, favicon and the QR rule exist as files; the QR rule shows a plain code with full quiet zone and nothing in the middle.
- [x] [ev:ci] The component sheet shows every listed state, including keyboard and gamepad focus.
- [x] [ev:ci] GUIDE.md names a reference image for each element and records the copy voice/glossary and the dim-room controller base.
- [x] [ev:ci] At least three H4-style frames (TV in-race grid with HUD, lobby at 32, phone controller) exist with committed prompts; generated vehicles/badges are marked placeholders; `ui_lobby.png` is marked superseded in MASTER_PROMPTS.
- [x] [ev:ci] A fresh-eyes review note (§13b.4) compares the style frames with H4. (The owner's judgement comes at P1-U04.)

title: P1-U01.3 · Design language rework: the owner's reference screens (R102)
description:
**Source:** `docs/playtests/poc-2026-10-03.md` (POC1-03); owner rulings R102 (`docs/policies/owner-direction-2026-09-29.md`). Rework of the closed parent br-p1-u01-mmq. **Drop:** `POC` · **Track:** `design` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** none (can start now). Blocks P1-U04.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Owner POC round 1: our guide ended up sterile with rounded corners on every element. Move toward the language of the four reference screens, not their content. The owner sees each change on the live POC at https://jammers-preview.dilger.dev/poc/ as soon as it is committed (CI/CD, P1-D03a), and reviews it there.

## Scope (owned paths)
`art/ui/GUIDE.md`, `art/ui/tokens.json` (+ schema), `art/ui/sheets/`, `art/ui/brand/` where the language touches them, `art/ui/poc/shared/`.

## Contract and design decisions
The owner's feedback, verbatim in intent (numbered as in `docs/playtests/poc-2026-10-03.md`; the acceptance below repeats it):
- **POC1-03** The guide, tokens and component sheet express: non-grid, hand-made placement; big images/renders as first-class elements; contrast banner backing for heading type; compact density; slants and high contrast that feel alive; colour behind some text; no uniform rounded corners on every element. It states what is taken from `art/ui/refs/owner-2026-10-03/` (language) and what is not (copy, vote cards, car art, mode names).
- **POC1-03** Tokens carry the new primitives (slant angle, banner styles, text-backing colours, corner rules) so the TV and phone mocks and the Rust/WASM UI can build from them; the existing checks (`check.mjs`, contrast, CVD sheet) pass on the new set.

Style and layout follow the owner's reference screens in `art/ui/refs/owner-2026-10-03/` for **language only, never content**. Present decisions, not option menus: one worked proposal with a one-line why (§3a). Anything the owner said they will send later (round 2) is out of scope until it arrives.

## Required tests
`art/ui/check.mjs` and the sheet renders; before/after captures of the component sheet next to the four reference screens, with a fresh-eyes review noting which of the owner's six points each capture shows. Evidence in `docs/evidence/P1-U01.3/`.

title: P1-U02 · TV mocks: grid, HUD, lobby and results
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-U02** (cites §3a items 2–7, 12, 14; §9; §10); master cut new (owner 2026-10-02); master §6.2, §6.3, §6.4, §10.6, §10.8 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `POC` · **Track:** `design` · **Machine:** `on:mac` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`, `ev:hardware`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-U01. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Show the owner, on the TCL from the couch, exactly how the TV will look before R04/R06/R07/R08/R09 build it: the grid as players
join and leave (1 → 32 → 1), grids with a gap, the per-tile HUD over **live moving tiles**, mixed FP/TP tiles, the lobby at
2/8/16/32, Minimum results, the host's own controls, caption placement, the over-3D overlays and (as a design reference only)
the derby Overview. The HUD is built the way the game will build it, so its frame cost is measured, not guessed. The accepted
mocks become the named references R-tasks are judged against.

## Scope (owned paths)
`art/ui/poc/tv/` (static HTML/CSS/JS built from `tokens.json`; three.js for the live tiles, bundled locally, no CDN).

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Phone mocks (U03); the in-world look and motion reel (U05; U05 renders on top of these mocks); the gallery/publication (U04). Building the derby Overview is Full (V2-22) and its scenarios (`derby-overview-8/24`) stay there.

## Contract and design decisions
Static HTML/CSS/JS layout mocks built from `tokens.json` at **1920×1080 and 3840×2160**, plus **21:9** and a **portrait phone host**
for the grid. They show §3a items 2–7, 12 and 14:
- a **grid player** that adds and removes players 1 → 32 → 1 with the animated reflow (seat order kept; only joins and leaves
  reflow, master §6.2), with the layout rule written next to it as **pseudocode** (it becomes P1-R04's contract once accepted).
  Master §6.2 rule to start from: choose rows × cols with rows·cols ≥ N minimising unused area, tile aspect in a playable band
  (~1.2–2.0 third person; FP a little narrower), any display aspect (portrait stacks vertically, ultrawide adds columns), spare
  cells show a filler (QR "join now", standings), never black; resizing animated (~300 ms ease) when N changes; for N = 2
  evaluate horizontal and vertical splits; playable area and own-car readability outrank filler panels;
- the **gap cases** N = 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 13 handled the §3a way (balanced rows; last row centred with wider tiles; leftovers show
  QR + standings);
- the **per-tile HUD**: number badge, name, position, lap, boost meter, wreck/respawn countdown, autopilot and reconnecting
  badges, Identify pulse and outline, the countdown overlay; at the smallest tile (32 tiles at 1080p) and the largest;
- **first- and third-person tiles mixed** in one grid (FP shows a bonnet edge, master §6.3);
- the **lobby** with the warm-up behind it at 2, 8, 16 and 32 players plus the rule for larger N (never a "max players");
- **Minimum results/intermission** at 8 and 32 players: race rematch, reel area, timer, QR, Hide replay / Start next round now /
  Return to lobby (H4's layout without Full's voting);
- the **host's own controls**: Start now, End and Disband with confirmation, pause, the pad/keyboard input drawer, the diagnostics
  overlay, and how they stay out of the way during a race;
- where the announcer's **captions** sit (A03) without covering anyone's HUD;
- the **overlays drawn over the 3D view**: nameplates over other cars, the Identify outline, the off-screen arrow to your own car;
- the **derby Overview** (master §6.4) as a forward design reference: a live greybox bowl with 8, 16 and 32 cars framed by the
  cars' bounding box at a fixed pitch (≈55–65°), never rotating; identity rings and nameplates scaled by camera distance; the HUD
  in thin edge bands (3-minute timer and damage-points standings); the host's Grid ↔ Overview switch. Design only.

**Tiles are live, never stills:** Spike J's Cruz Missile (`spikes/art-pipeline/J-cruze-lowpoly/`) driving scripted laps in three.js
on a greybox loop and one biome backdrop, so the HUD is judged over moving dust, debris and sky. Stills appear only in captures;
never generated cars. The HUD is built the game's way (DEFAULT: DOM/CSS overlays positioned over each tile's viewport, one layer
for all tiles), so its cost is known before C/R tasks commit to it. Every state opens from a **URL fragment** (for the owner and
for the capture script). No CDN (R70).

§3a starting proposals (DEFAULT; the POC designs and shows each as ONE worked proposal with a one-line why; owner
2026-10-03: "don't give me choices on things that are obvious"; alternatives stay in evidence folders, not the gallery):
- Lobby: the warm-up drive behind the QR and player strip (plan §9).
- Grids with a gap: balanced rows first; the last row is centred and its tiles grow wider within the aspect band, so gameplay
  area comes first (master §6.2); any cell still left over shows the join QR and live standings, never black.
- Cameras: third person by default, first person per seat from the controller (master §6.3); mocks show a mixed grid.
- In-world look: master §12.1's comic treatment (faceted cars, 2–3 tone toon ramp, ink outlines, halftone in shadows); if its
  cost at 24 tiles is too high, present the cheapest version that keeps the look (e.g. outlines on cars and debris only) and say why.
- Controller in a dark room: ink/navy base with cream panels and the player's colour; the TV keeps H4's cream panels.
- Lobby at 32 and beyond: compact roster cards (number badge, colour, name, Ready) that reflow into more columns down to the
  guide's legible minimum, then compact to number + name chips. Never a "max players".

## Interfaces
- Consumes: `art/ui/tokens.json`, fonts and components from P1-U01; Spike J's model script (evidence folder, imported by the mock only).
- Provides: the grid pseudocode → P1-R04; HUD layout/cost → P1-R07; lobby/results layouts → P1-R07; host controls → P1-R07/C05;
  caption placement → P1-A03; the TV base the motion reel and world look (P1-U05) render on; captures for the gallery (P1-U04).

## Reuses / gap
Reuses Spike J's model and its 24×24 bench (`spikes/art-pipeline/J-cruze-lowpoly/REPORT.md`). Gap: no TV HUD, reflow, gap, FP/TP-mix, 32-lobby or host-controls reference existed (plan T65).

Let the owner judge thumb reach and legibility on a phone (only possible on a phone) before P1-C02/C03/C06/C07 build the

(M2), a tutorial prompt and every §11 controller state, in device frames at true CSS sizes and as a **live mock** on the owner's
own phone.

## Scope (owned paths)
`art/ui/poc/phone/` (static HTML/CSS/JS from `tokens.json`; no Three.js).

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The real controller app (P1-C02), join flow (C03), scanner (C04), tutorial (C06) and settings (C07). Nothing here sends network traffic.

## Contract and design decisions
- **In-race controller** (M2 in `docs/plans/ux-study-2026-09-29/`): DRIVE stick left, ACTION stick right (R60), with the boost meter,
  wheelie preload and utility ready/cooldown indicators next to the sticks; secondary buttons away from thumbs: Identify,
  camera (chase/first person), Recover, Help, Settings, Leave; the HUD strip. Identify is also the first entry in the controller menu, and
  its full-screen flash (the number, big, in the player's colour) is one of the mocked states.
- Also: lobby with READY, join (M1: code entry + Scan QR code side by side), settings (M2), a tutorial prompt, and **every §11
  controller state**: Finding the game, No such game, Game ended, Preview expired, Connecting, Finding a relay, No route, Ready
  to join, Joining, Playing ("You're #12"), Reconnecting ("Reconnecting as #12…"), Host gone, Host paused, Another tab, Update needed.
- **Portrait and landscape**, in device frames at true CSS sizes: small iPhone 375×667, large iPhone 430×932, mid Android 412×915
  (DEFAULT set).
- **Live mock** on the owner's phone (served over HTTPS from the POC gallery): sticks follow the thumbs and drive the indicators,
  the §11 edge-safe zones are visible (stick zones start ≥ 24 px from screen edges because iOS Safari's edge swipe navigates
  back), a thumb-reach overlay toggles, and nothing is sent anywhere.
- Each stick's states: idle, touched, wheelie preload, utility cooldown, disabled, on autopilot; press/release feedback.
- Uses the **dark-room base** (§3a: ink/navy base, cream panels, the player's colour).
- Touch hygiene matches §11 so the mock behaves like the real thing: `touch-action: none`, no pinch/double-tap zoom, no selection.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: tokens/fonts/components from P1-U01.
- Provides: accepted phone layouts → P1-C02 (sticks/HUD), C03 (states/wording), C06 (prompt), C07 (settings); captures → P1-U04.
