comments.text:
Owner phone screenshot, 2026-10-03 23:46 (Brave on Android, landscape, https://jammers-preview.dilger.dev/poc/phone/). Fold into this bead's acceptance; each item is checked in the device-frame captures and on the live mock.

1. POC1-22 (fullscreen) is NOT met on the owner's phone. The URL bar, the status bar and the bottom tab strip are all visible, and there is no fullscreen prompt on screen. The AC text "the live mock does both on the owner's phone" is wrong for Brave/Android: don't carry it over. Required: a tap-to-go-fullscreen prompt on first load and after any exit from fullscreen; the wake lock is requested from the same gesture; a stated fallback when requestFullscreen is unavailable (iOS Safari: Add-to-Home-Screen hint; Brave: verify the API actually works). Playwright asserts the prompt shows when not fullscreen and goes away after the tap. Check in Brave on a real Android phone, not only Chromium.
2. POC1-18 (centre top) is not met: the Boost bar and the "Cone ready" item are inside the right-hand ACTION panel, not centred between the two sides.
3. Layout bug: the Boost bar and the cone button overlap the "ACTION" panel label, so the label is unreadable. Nothing may overlap a panel label at any phone size, in portrait or landscape.
4. The "Mock ▾" selector sits inside the ACTION panel and hides part of it. Keep it mock-only and move it where it can't cover a control or the HUD.
5. The top bar crowds right-hand controls: the Identify, camera and reset buttons touch and the cone overlaps the camera and reset buttons. Give the controls tap-safe spacing (R101) and keep Identify as the one prominent control.
6. The drive and action zones leave a large empty strip below the sticks; use the landscape height (bigger stick travel area) now that fullscreen will add height.

comments.author: cdilga
comments.text:
Owner follow-up (2026-10-03): the controller needs an OBVIOUS fullscreen button, in addition to the first-load prompt in the previous comment. Added to POC1-22:
- A persistent, clearly labelled fullscreen button in the top bar (icon plus the word "Fullscreen"), visible whenever the page is not fullscreen; it toggles, and swaps to an exit-fullscreen icon when active. Tap-safe size and spacing (R101).
- The same tap requests the wake lock (after the fullscreen call). If the user exits fullscreen, the button and the prompt come back.
- Where fullscreen is unsupported (iOS Safari), the button shows the Add-to-Home-Screen hint instead of doing nothing.
- Playwright: button visible when not fullscreen, hidden or toggled when fullscreen, wake-lock call follows the tap. Capture it in the device-frame shots and on the owner's Brave/Android phone.

comments.author: cdilga
comments.text:
Owner correction (2026-10-03), supersedes the wake-lock line in the previous comment: the wake lock is independent of the fullscreen button. Without it the phone can sleep before the player goes fullscreen.
- Request the wake lock as early as possible: on joining (the Join tap is a user gesture, so it is the natural moment), not on the fullscreen tap. The Screen Wake Lock API does not strictly need a gesture in Chromium, so also try on page load and retry on the first tap anywhere if it was refused.
- The lock is released whenever the tab is hidden or the screen locks, so re-acquire on visibilitychange (visible), after fullscreen enter/exit, and on any release event. Hold it for the whole session (lobby, tutorial, race, intermission), release on leaving the room.
- Fullscreen stays a separate, optional button. Neither depends on the other.
- Unsupported or refused: show a small "screen may sleep" notice and keep retrying on taps; on iOS, the Add-to-Home-Screen hint covers it.
- Playwright: wake-lock request is made on join without any fullscreen tap, and is re-made after a visibility change. Verify on the owner's Brave/Android phone that the screen stays on through an idle lobby.

comments.author: cdilga
comments.text:
Owner clarification (2026-10-03), refines the wake-lock comment above: the purpose of the wake lock is connection stability. A controller that sleeps drops out of the match or disconnects, and we want it to stay connected. Judge the design by that goal, not by a fixed trigger.
- WHEN to acquire, hold and release is the implementing agent's call. "On join, hold for the whole session" in the previous comment is a starting proposal, not a mandate. State the chosen policy and its one-line why in the evidence.
- Evidence that it serves the goal: on the owner's Brave/Android phone, leave the controller idle in a room past the device's screen-timeout and show it stays connected (no sleep, no drop), plus a reconnect check for when the lock is lost (tab hidden or screen locked): the controller re-acquires and rejoins cleanly.
- Fullscreen stays independent of it.

title: P1-U05 · In-world look and motion
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-U05** (cites §3a items 9, 10, 13); master cut new (owner 2026-10-03); master §12.1, §12.1a, §6.3 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `POC` · **Track:** `design` · **Machine:** `on:mac` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:hardware`, `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-U01, P1-U02, P1-F11. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
H4 is a painting and the game renders a faceted low-poly car, so the chrome and the world have to be shown together. Render
the in-world look live with the real Cruz Missile under U02's HUD, measure its frame cost at 24 tiles, draw the in-world graphics
in that look, and build a live motion reel with reduced-motion variants. The accepted look is what P1-R10 puts into the engine.

## Scope (owned paths)
`art/ui/poc/world/`, `art/ui/poc/motion/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Implementing the look in the game renderer (P1-R10); the grid/HUD layouts themselves (P1-U02).

## Contract and design decisions
**(1) The in-world look.** Live in three.js, the real Cruz Missile (Spike J's model) on the greybox and one biome backdrop, under
U02's HUD, at TV size, in a 24-tile grid and in U02's Overview bowl, in the §3a look (master §12.1): faceted with a **2–3 tone toon
ramp**, **ink outlines** (screen-space edge detection on depth + normals + object ID, run once in post) and **halftone in the
shadows**, with a touch of §12.1a's sun-bleached grit. Comic effects never cover identity (number/colour) or the road ahead.
Build it with the vendored shader skills and the `jammers-look` adapter (P1-F11). Measure its frame cost at 24 tiles on the Mac (an outline pass per tile viewport is the likely expense). If too high, find the
cheapest version that keeps the look (e.g. outlines on cars and debris only) and present that, with why.

**(2) In-world graphics** in that look: checkpoint gate and finish-line markers, route edges and barrier colours, wayfinding
chevrons, and how each identity colour reads as **lit paint on the car next to its flat badge**.

**(3) Motion reel**, built live on U02's mocks so timings are real (not a video edit): the countdown, a join (tile appears, grid
reflows), the Identify pulse (master §5.2: ~1.5 s pulse/scale, "#7 THAT'S YOU!" burst, outline in other tiles), a wreck and
respawn (respawn cuts, never swoops), the phase changes (lobby → countdown → race → results) and the results reveal. Each has a
**reduced-motion version** (removes excess shake/flashes without reducing information); durations come from U01's tokens.

§3a starting proposals (DEFAULT; the POC designs and shows each as ONE worked proposal with a one-line why; owner
2026-10-03: "don't give me choices on things that are obvious"; alternatives stay in evidence folders, not the gallery):
- Lobby: the warm-up drive behind the QR and player strip (plan §9).
- Grids with a gap: balanced rows first; the last row is centred and its tiles grow wider within the aspect band, so gameplay
  area comes first (master §6.2); any cell still left over shows the join QR and live standings, never black.
- Cameras: third person by default, first person per seat from the controller (master §6.3); mocks show a mixed grid.
- In-world look: master §12.1's comic treatment (faceted cars, 2–3 tone toon ramp, ink outlines, halftone in shadows); if its
  cost at 24 tiles is too high, present the cheapest version that keeps the look (e.g. outlines on cars and debris only) and say why.
- Controller in a dark room: ink/navy base with cream panels and the player's colour; the TV keeps H4's cream panels.
- Lobby at 32 and beyond: compact roster cards (number badge, colour, name, Ready) that reflow into more columns down to the
  guide's legible minimum, then compact to number + name chips. Never a "max players".

## Interfaces
- Consumes: tokens (U01), the TV mocks and HUD (U02), Spike J's model.
- Provides: accepted world-look frames + cost table → P1-R10 (its frame-cost budget is U05's measurement + 20 %); the identity
  paint-vs-badge check → R10; motion timings → R04 (reflow), R06 (Identify), R07 (phase changes), R09 (results reveal).

## Reuses / gap
Reuses Spike J's model and bench. Gap: nothing showed the painted references and the faceted renderer together.

## Required tests
- Headed Mac GPU frame-cost measurement at 24 tiles for the full look and any cheaper variant (p50/p95/p99, browser + backend).
- A side-by-side capture of every identity palette entry as lit paint next to its flat badge.
- A screen recording of the reel at token durations and in reduced motion.
- Fresh-eyes review note comparing with H4.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
Captures + frame-cost table + a screen recording of the reel + review note. Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-U05/`.

## How this bead closes
- `ev:hardware`: a perf/network receipt naming hardware, browser/backend, build and cohort, closed through the evidence close (`batch-verify.sh close <id> --evidence <file>`, P1-F02).
- `ev:ci`: green Gitea CI on a commit containing this bead, cited as `receipt:<run url>` with a `batch_verify` gate pass (before CI exists, a committed local receipt; while CI is down, the verifier's `batch-verify.sh` receipt).

description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-V01** (cites §6.1, §6.2, §13b.2); master cut V2-61 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).

## Purpose and observable outcome
A machine-checked contract for vehicle assets: the sidecar schema and a GLB validator that checks the GLB data itself (not just sidecar
claims), exposed as `jj validate`. It catches the spike-era mistakes (mass fractions summing to 0.92, origin off the ground, a "round" cabin
proxy that was a box).

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-contracts/`, `art/contracts/vehicle.schema.json`, `jj validate` in `crates/jj-tools/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Baking the Cruze (V02); maps in `jj validate` (M01 adds them).

## Contract and design decisions
Sidecar (`<vehicle>.asset.json`, plan §6.2): units metres, forward axis, origin on the ground between the axles; parts `core`, `front`,
`back`, `door_FL/FR/RL/RR`, `wheel_FL/FR/RL/RR`, each with pivot, **hinge axis + loose limits**, mass fraction (**sum 1 ± 0.01**),
collider proxy (convex/cuboid/capsule); anchors `cam_fp`, `cam_tp_target`, `com`, `roof_number`, `lplate_front`, `lplate_rear`. One material;
the atlas carries the paint key.
Validator checks GLB data: part IDs present **at every LOD** (names and pivots identical across LODs), pivots, hinge axes and limits, mass sum,
origin on the ground, the rounded cabin proxy isn't a cuboid, anchors present, triangle/material/draw counts against budgets
(≤ ~1.3k / 0.9k / 0.6k tris). `jj validate FILE` with `--json`; exits non-zero naming the failed rule.

## Interfaces
- Provides: `jj validate` + schema to V02 (bake), V03, CI `tools` lane, `vehicle-model-validation` skill.

## Required tests
- A small hand-made valid fixture (GLB + sidecar) passes; ten deliberately broken fixtures each fail with a named rule.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
Validator output both ways. (Passing the baked Cruze is P1-V02's acceptance; V01 can't depend on its own consumer.) Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-V01/`.

title: P1-W01 · Item system: cards, a two-slot queue and use
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-W01** (cites master §9.2, §9.3; owner 2026-10-03); master cut V2-70 slice (owner 2026-10-03) (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D7` · **Track:** `items` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-S08, P1-S04, P1-S05, P1-N06. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
The shared item system the boomerang and the sanga plug into: versioned item cards, a two-slot queue per car used in order, and use on the ACTION stick.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-sim/src/items/`, `assets/items/*.json` (cards), card validator in `jj-contracts`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The two items (W02, W03); pickup stations and boxes (W04); HUD and journeys (W05).

## Contract and design decisions
Owner direction 2026-10-03: before the full test after Playtest 1, the game has **one weapon and one boost-type item**: the
**boomerang** and the **"sanga"** (a sausage on bread). Each player stores **two items, used in the order they were picked up**. Other item
ideas wait (master §9.5's list). Pickups look like **delivery boxes** with the item printed on the outside (R94).
Rules carried from master §9.2: one shared ACTION vertical gesture uses the front item; self-use items work in either vertical direction;
respawn clears held items (no free pickup); spawn-protected cars can't collect or use offensive items; a failed use keeps the item and says
why; fired items keep their causal owner through the owner's respawn and expire naturally or at round end; round-end cleanup removes effects
in the retired world, never live debris; every item lists its counterplay; effects are forces, zones or bounded changes, never scripted poses;
damage goes through the part model (S04).

- **Cards as data** (`assets/items/<id>.json`, validated): id, version, class (projectile/buff), activation (sector entry), direction
  (forward/rear/self), uses, arming, lifetime/duration, cleanup policy, counterplay list (a card without counterplay is rejected), presentation
  hooks, rationale.
- **Two-slot queue per car:** pickups fill the back; ACTION up or down uses the front item and the queue shifts (owner 2026-10-03). A full
  queue doesn't consume a pickup.
- With an empty queue, ACTION up/down keep P1-S08's OI! flash and cone (DEFAULT, harmless fallback); the wire stays the same
  (`utilityForward`/`utilityRear` mean "use forward/rear").
- Damage from items goes through S04's parts; in derby it's credited to the item's owner (S10 attribution).

## Interfaces
- Consumes: S08 actions, S04 damage, S05 respawn/race state, N06. Provides: the item framework to W02–W05, inventory in snapshots/HUD facts.

## Required tests
- Scenarios: queue order, full-queue pass-through, respawn clears, protected car can't use offensive items, failed use keeps the item, round-end cleanup, replay determinism; card validator rejects missing fields or counterplay.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
Scenario output. Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-W01/`.

The first weapon: a boomerang you throw forward or back that arcs out, hits cars on the way out and back, and returns to you.

  hit), and 25 damage to the part it strikes (S04). Sanga'd cars take ×0.2 (W03).
- Walls, terrain and debris stop or deflect it (counterplay); the thrower catches it on return with no effect; uncaught, it drops and expires.

title: P1-W03 · Sanga: the tank-up buff
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-W03** (cites owner 2026-10-03; master §9.2); master cut new (owner 2026-10-03) (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D7` · **Track:** `items` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-W01. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
The first boost-type item (owner 2026-10-03): eat a sanga and for a while you shrug off weapons and other cars: you can tank them and just
drive without worrying about their collisions.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-sim/src/items/sanga.rs`, `assets/items/sanga.json`, `scenarios/items/`, `web/host/src/render/items/sanga/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The framework (W01), pickups (W04).

## Contract and design decisions
Card defaults (TUNE):
- Self-use in either vertical direction; lasts **6 s**; using another sanga while one is active refreshes the timer (no stacking multiplier).
- **Tank:** the car's rigid body gets a higher Rapier dominance group than other cars and debris for the duration, so contacts push them and
  not it (DEFAULT approach; verify the rapier3d 0.36 API and record it). Terrain and barriers still collide normally.
- **Shrug off:** contact damage to it is ignored for the duration; weapon effects on it are ×0.2 (the boomerang's impulse and damage).
- Its own driving is unchanged (no speed boost); it still deals damage when it rams (credited normally in derby).
- Ends at a tick boundary; if it overlaps another car at the end, the separation adds no launch (energy accounting).
- Looks: a warm emissive aura and a sizzle of steam (R12 system), a timer on the controller and the tile.
- Counterplay: it's timed and visible; terrain, barriers and the bowl still matter.

## Required tests
- Scenarios: tank-push (pushes a stationary car aside keeping ≥ 90 % of its speed), ram-immunity (rammed at 15 m/s: no damage and a small heading change), vs-boomerang (×0.2), ends-cleanly (no launch on expiry overlap, energy check), refresh-not-stack.

title: P1-U02 bug · Grid visual layout broken on phone viewport (logic OK)
description:
**Source:** owner review of `https://jammers-preview.dilger.dev/poc/tv/#grid` on a phone (portrait, Android Brave), 2026-10-04. Related: P1-R04 (grid layout kernel), P1-R08 (any-aspect and phone host), P1-U02.

## Finding
The grid **logic is right** (the count, the rows, which tile goes where). The **visual display is broken** on a phone-sized host viewport: per-tile HUD cards (position + "Lap 1/3" + progress bar) overlap each other and spill past the tile edges, tiles overlap in the lower rows (two screens drawn on top of each other), cream "empty" tiles stack under live ones, and the whole grid sits in a small box in the middle of a large blank area instead of using the viewport.

## Fix
- Tile HUD scales with its tile (container-relative sizing), never wider than the tile; text truncates or reflows before it overlaps a neighbour.
- Tiles never overlap and never exceed the grid rect, at any viewport size and aspect (phone portrait included).
- The grid uses the whole usable viewport.
- No cap on tile count: this is layout only, count stays unlimited (R-ruling).

## Acceptance
- Playwright Chromium + WebKit at 360x800, 390x844, 412x915 portrait and landscape, and TV 1920x1080, for 1, 4, 12, 24 and 40 tiles: no two tile rects intersect, every HUD box is inside its tile, grid area covers at least 90% of the viewport's usable area.
- A screenshot of each case is looked at by the agent before closing (see self-look loop below), and attached under `docs/evidence/<id>/`.
- Anti-narrowing: no tile-count cap, no hiding tiles to make it fit.

## Self-look loop (applies to every design bead)
Before closing, run `node art/ui/lib/live-check.mjs` against the deployed preview (fails on 4xx, undecoded images, uncaught errors, and saves screenshots), then open the screenshots and look at them. Broken images and overlaps get fixed before the owner sees them.

title: P1-U02 · Host QR and player list: maximise QR, hide it later, maximise game area
description:
**Source:** owner review of the new grid layout on a phone, 2026-10-04. Related: P1-R04, P1-R08, P1-U02.4 (warm-up/lobby).

## Finding
The grid is great overall. Two space problems on the host screen:
1. The **QR code** (it substitutes in dynamically) is smaller than the space it could use, and it **hides too early** as players join.
2. When the **player list** is also shown, the layout wastes space. Both the QR and the player list should be sized to maximise the **single-player (game) window area** whenever either is present.

## Fix
- The QR takes the largest square the free space allows (bounded below by reliable scanning distance), growing back as space frees up. It stays visible for as long as it physically fits at scannable size; it hides only when it cannot fit at that size, not at a fixed player count or timer.
- QR and player list share a layout solver with the grid: allocate the chrome (QR + list) the minimum it needs, give everything else to the game tiles, in every aspect (TV landscape, phone portrait, ultrawide).
- Player list never imposes a count limit (scrolls/columns, never truncates).

## Acceptance
- Playwright at TV 1920x1080, 1366x768, phone portrait 390x844 and landscape 844x390: with QR only, list only, both, and neither, for 1, 8, 24 and 60 players: game area is maximal (chrome takes no more than its minimum plus margins), QR >= minimum scannable size whenever any free rect fits it, nothing overlaps.
- QR scan check: decode the captured QR with a decoder at each size and assert the room URL.
- Screenshots reviewed by the agent before close (self-look loop: `node art/ui/lib/live-check.mjs`).
- Anti-narrowing: no player cap, no hiding the list to make space.
